exposure: Maternal 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25OHD) status in early (T1) and late (T3) pregnancy
cohort: Participants in the GraviD study, consisting of pregnant women whose vitamin D status was measured, and their children who were followed up to 5 years of age for atopic diseases.
finding: Among children without reported atopic heredity, higher maternal vitamin D status and intake during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of reported atopic disease (asthma, eczema, and food allergy).
